title: 3.6 Levels of Biological Organization
description: The hierarchical organization of life from cells to the biosphere

questions.question: What is the simplest (lowest) level of biological organization?
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life and is considered the simplest level of biological organization.

questions.question: What is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function called?
questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function (e.g., muscle tissue, nervous tissue).

questions.question: What is a group of different tissues working together to perform a specific function called?
questions.explanation: An organ is a structure composed of two or more tissue types working together to perform a specific function (e.g., heart, liver).

questions.question: What is a group of organs that work together to carry out a major life function called?
questions.explanation: An organ system is a group of organs that work together to perform a major life function (e.g., digestive system, respiratory system).

questions.question: What is a complete, living individual organism called at the organism level?
questions.explanation: An organism is an individual living thing that can carry out all life processes independently.

questions.question: What is a group of individuals of the same species living in the same area called?
questions.explanation: A population is a group of individuals of the same species that live in the same geographic area and can interbreed.

questions.question: What is a group of different populations of different species living and interacting in the same area called?
questions.explanation: A community (or biological community) consists of all the populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

questions.question: What is the combination of a community and its non-living (abiotic) environment called?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes both the living (biotic) community and the non-living (abiotic) factors such as water, soil, air, and sunlight.

questions.question: What is a large geographic area characterized by a specific climate and dominant plant types called?
questions.explanation: A biome is a large geographic region with a specific climate, plant life, and animal life (e.g., tropical rainforest, desert, tundra).

questions.question: What is the highest (most comprehensive) level of biological organization?
questions.explanation: The biosphere is the highest level — it includes all ecosystems and biomes on Earth where life exists (land, water, and atmosphere).

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of biological organization from simplest to most complex?
options: Organism → Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Population → Community → Ecosystem → Biome → Biosphere
Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Organism → Population → Community → Ecosystem → Biome → Biosphere
Cell → Organ → Tissue → Organ System → Organism → Community → Population → Ecosystem → Biosphere → Biome
Tissue → Cell → Organ → Organ System → Organism → Population → Community → Biome → Ecosystem → Biosphere
questions.explanation: The correct order: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Organism → Population → Community → Ecosystem → Biome → Biosphere.

questions.question: At which level of organization do heart muscle cells belong?
questions.explanation: Individual heart muscle cells belong to the cell level of biological organization.

questions.question: At which level of organization does cardiac muscle tissue belong?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle (a group of similar heart muscle cells working together) is at the tissue level.

questions.question: At which level of organization does the human heart belong?
questions.explanation: The heart is an organ — it is made of different tissues (cardiac muscle, nervous tissue, connective tissue) working together to pump blood.

questions.question: At which level of organization does the circulatory system belong?
questions.explanation: The circulatory system is an organ system — it consists of the heart (organ), blood vessels (organs), and blood (tissue) working together.

questions.question: A single lion living in the savanna is at which level of biological organization?
questions.explanation: A single individual lion is at the organism level.

questions.question: A pride of lions living in the same savanna region represents which level?
questions.explanation: A pride of lions (same species, same area) represents a population.

questions.question: Lions, zebras, giraffes, and grasses all living together in a savanna represent which level?
questions.explanation: Multiple different species (lions, zebras, giraffes, grasses) living together form a community.

questions.question: The savanna including its soil, water, sunlight, and all living organisms represents which level?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes both the living community and the abiotic (non-living) factors like soil, water, and sunlight.

questions.question: The tropical savanna as a large geographic region with distinct climate and vegetation is called a:
questions.explanation: The tropical savanna is a biome — a large geographic region characterized by a specific climate (warm with wet/dry seasons) and plant life (grasses with scattered trees).

questions.question: All the water on Earth, including oceans, lakes, and rivers, is part of which level?
questions.explanation: All water bodies are part of the hydrosphere, which is a component of the biosphere — the global sum of all ecosystems.

questions.question: Which level of organization consists of all ecosystems on Earth?
questions.explanation: The biosphere is the global sum of all ecosystems, encompassing all living organisms and their environments on Earth.

questions.question: What defines a population versus a community?
options: A population includes abiotic factors; a community does not
A population is one species; a community includes multiple species
A population is larger than a community
questions.explanation: A population consists of individuals of a single species. A community consists of multiple populations of different species interacting.

questions.question: Which level of organization is a school of fish (same species) in a lake?
questions.explanation: A school of fish of the same species in a lake represents a population.

questions.question: A leaf is at which level of biological organization?
questions.explanation: A leaf is an organ — it is composed of different tissues (epidermis, mesophyll, vascular tissue) working together for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which level includes both living and non-living components?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes both biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) components such as water, sunlight, soil, and temperature.

questions.question: Which level is made up of only one species?
questions.explanation: A population consists of individuals of only one species living in the same area.

questions.question: The nervous system is an example of which level of organization?
questions.explanation: The nervous system is an organ system — it includes the brain, spinal cord, and nerves working together.

questions.question: Blood is classified at which level of biological organization?
questions.explanation: Blood is classified as connective tissue — a group of similar cells (red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets) in a fluid matrix.

questions.question: The human body as a whole represents which level of biological organization?
questions.explanation: A complete individual human being is at the organism level — the highest level of individual organization.
